To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the viral genome of the different viral particles and structures is spatially linked and that viral DNA is spatially linked to the viral 72 k protein and to the internal nuclear matrix.
the viral genome and cellular chromatin remain compartmentalized throughout the adenovirus infection, even when viral DNA is released from the viral capsid.

(i) cellular DNA is restricted to the cellular chromosomes, (ii) viral DNA is confined to the virus-induced regions, (iii) viral DNA is spatially linked, and (iv) the viral ssDNA accumulation site is a matrix-associated, pleomorphic, and topologically localized structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the distribution of viral genomes within the cell nucleus.
the study of the compartmentalization of cellular DNA and virus DNA in Ad5-infected HeLa cells using a combination of ultrastructuralin situ and immunocytochemical techniques.
the compartmentalization of viral and cellular DNA during the adenovirus life cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the viral DNA of adenovirus type-5 is compartmentalized within a network of nuclear matrix proteins.
the viral genomes are confined to the virus-induced regions and are not interpenetrated within the cellular chromatin.
cellular and viral DNas are topologically segregated during the entire Ad5 infectious cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

viral and cellular DNA are separated in the nucleus of infected cells, and that viral DNA is compartmentalized in the nucleus of the infected cells, and the viral DNA is compartmented in the nucleus of virus-induced regions.
Ad5 viral DNA is compartmentalized in the infected nuclei.
the viral DNA is compartmentalized and segregated from cellular chromatin, which is in accordance with the concept of a nuclear sub-compartment for virus replication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the virus genome is not free to move in the infected cell.
the virus genome is compartmentalized within the infected cell, and this compartmentalization is a prerequisite for virus replication and assembly.
the viral genome, as well as the viral proteins, are compartmentalized into discrete structures in the infected nuclei.
